summary: What the bell opens: notifications grouped by day — Today, Yesterday, Earlier — with unread ones marked in words as well as a dot, a read toggle on each that never disappears, Mark all as read, an empty state and a loading state. Content for a Popover or a Drawer; the caller owns the data.
useWhen: the product tells a user about things that happened while they were elsewhere — an approval waiting, a run that failed, a mention
each item can be opened, and whether it has been seen matters

useInstead.when: the result of what the user just did — saved, sent, deleted
useInstead.why: it comes and goes by itself; a notification waits in the list

useInstead.when: a notice about the whole product — maintenance, a trial ending
useInstead.why: it is seen on every page without opening anything

useInstead.when: the history of one record — who changed it and when
useInstead.why: an activity log has nothing to mark as read; Timeline, when it ships, is the record's history

composition.note: The bell is a Button whose name says the count — "Notifications, 3 unread" — and opens a Popover titled Notifications, lg, whose content is the panel. On a phone use a Drawer instead. The caller keeps the list and updates it from `onReadChange` and `onMarkAllRead`; `href` makes a title a link, `onOpen` a button. With `notifications` empty it shows "You’re all caught up"; with `isLoading`, rows of Skeleton and "Loading notifications" announced.
composition.example: <Popover title="Notifications" size="lg" content={<NotificationsPanel notifications={items} onReadChange={setRead} onMarkAllRead={readAll} />}><Button aria-label="Notifications, 3 unread" … /></Popover>

requires: the container's name — the Popover's or Drawer's `title`, "Notifications"
the bell's name includes the unread count, since its badge is not read
`labels` — translated, with `unread` as a function of the count
guarantees: an unread notification's title begins "Unread:" for a screen reader; the dot and weight are not the only signal
the unread count is in words in the bar
each group is a section named by its heading, so a screen reader can jump between days
each toggle stays where it is and swaps Mark as read for Mark as unread — focus is never on something that vanishes
Mark all as read moves focus to the first notification before it goes
every change is announced in a status region that is always mounted
groups are counted from the local calendar day, not 24-hour windows; each has a machine-readable <time>
notes: opening an unread notification marks it read, through `onReadChange`
the list scrolls inside the panel past 28rem, so the popover never runs off the screen

antiPatterns.dont: a blue dot as the only sign a notification is unread
antiPatterns.do: NotificationsPanel, which also says "Unread:" and counts them
antiPatterns.why: a dot is silent to a screen reader and missing in forced colours
the badge's number is not part of the name that is read

antiPatterns.dont: a Mark as read button that is removed once pressed
antiPatterns.do: the panel's toggle, which becomes Mark as unread
antiPatterns.why: removing the focused button sends a keyboard user to the top of the page
